# NOTE: `langchain` bare is NOT imported anywhere. Only the subpackages below are.
#
# langchain-community is a TRANSITIVE dependency of ragas, so it has no import
# anywhere in this repo — but it must still be pinned. ragas 0.2.15 does
# `from langchain_community.chat_models.vertexai import ChatVertexAI`
# (ragas/llms/base.py:8), and that module was deleted in langchain-community
# 0.4.2. Without this pin a clean install resolves the newest release and
# src/evaluation/ragas_evaluator.py becomes unimportable.
#
# This was previously listed as "unused" based on a 0-import scan. That check is
# wrong for transitive dependencies.

# ── ORCHESTRATION (LangGraph) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# STATUS: declared + installed, but NOT YET WIRED INTO src/.
#
# ⚠️ CONFLICT WITH PROJECT_GOALS.md §9 "Non-Goals":
#    - "Generic LLM wrapper"      -> LangGraph is one
#    - "Single-turn QA"           -> LangGraph is a stateful graph engine
#    - "Global mutable state"     -> langgraph-checkpoint implies persistence
#
# The project already ships a hand-rolled orchestrator:
#    src/controller/agent.py           (loop + _decide_next_action)
#    src/controller/policy_engine.py   (routing)
#    src/controller/confidence_engine.py
#    src/controller/agent_state.py
#
# Wiring LangGraph in means TWO orchestrators competing for control, which is
# an architecture redesign — outside the Phase A–J scope.
# It is declared here for isolated evaluation only. Do not import it in src/
# without an explicit decision record.
#
# See: results/metrics/fase_j_confidence_dataset_architecture.md
langgraph==1.2.12

# pandas               : not imported directly; only ragas `to_pandas()`

#                        to archive/legacy_2026_10/retrieval/embedder.py
# ollama               : hard-imported by the legacy evaluator, which had 0
#                        inbound imports. Archived to
#                        archive/legacy_2026_10/evaluation/evaluator.py
# requests             : scripts/run_eval_ragas.py only
# langchain-google-genai : guarded by try/except (GEMINI_AVAILABLE flag)
#
# ── RESOLVED — was previously misdiagnosed here ────────────────────────────────
# An earlier version of this file attributed four test failures to a
# "numpy 2.5.3 / Python 3.14 incompatibility". That was wrong, and the numpy
# error message is misleading. Real cause, reproduced in isolation:
#
#   unittest.mock.patch.dict(sys.modules, ...) snapshots sys.modules and
#   restores it wholesale on exit, so any module first imported *inside* the
#   block is evicted. numpy.fft._pocketfft_umath is a C extension, and CPython
#   forbids initialising the same extension twice in one process — hence
#   "ImportError: cannot load module more than once per process". sklearn and
#   transformers both pull numpy.fft in through the patched import, which is why
#   a test that passed alone failed inside the full suite.
#
# Fix: pre-import numpy.fft above the patch.dict block so it lands in the
# snapshot. Both affected files now do this.
#
# This is a test-harness defect, NOT a numpy or Python 3.14 defect, and is
# unrelated to src/_compat.py (which handles a separate protobuf upb problem).
#
# Test baseline at this commit: 166 passed, 0 failed. No --ignore flags needed.
# See tests/test_qdrant_store.py and tests/test_semantic_chunker.py.
# =============================================================================
